chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to me, from their two fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja’far, from his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his brother al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: Amir al-Mu’minin (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful” is a verse from the Opening of the Book, and it consists of seven verses, the completion of which is “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” I heard the Messenger of God (may God’s blessings be upon him and his family) saying: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, said to me: “O Muhammad! We have given you the Seven Oft-Repeated and the Great Quran.”

So He singled out the favour upon me through the Opening of the Book and placed it equal to the Great Quran. Indeed, the Opening of the Book is the most noble of what is in the treasures of the Throne. And indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, chose Muhammad specifically and honoured him with it, and did not share it with any of His prophets, except Sulayman (peace be upon him), for He gave him from it “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.”

Do you not see that He relates about Bilqis when she said: “Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me. Indeed it is from Sulayman, and indeed it reads: In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful”?

Indeed, whoever recites it whilst believing in the allegiance to Muhammad and his righteous family, submitting to their command, and believing in their apparent and hidden teachings, God, Mighty and Majestic, will give him for every letter of it a good deed, each one better for him than the world and all that is in it of its wealth and goodness. And whoever listens to a reciter reciting it will have the equivalent of one-third of the reciter’s reward. So let each of you increase from this good that is offered to you, for it is a treasure -- do not let its time pass away, lest regret remain in your hearts.

key_terms.المثاني: Al-Mathani -- The Oft-Repeated, referring to the seven verses of al-Fatiha as mentioned in Quran 15:87
key_terms.فاتحة الكتاب: Fatihat al-Kitab -- The Opening of the Book, Surah al-Fatiha, the first chapter of the Quran
key_terms.كنوز العرش: Kunuz al-Arsh -- Treasures of the Throne, the most precious divine endowments stored near the Divine Throne
key_terms.موالاة: Muwalat -- Allegiance and loyalty to the Prophet and his family, a central tenet in Shia theology

ai.seo_question: Is Bismillah a verse of Surah al-Fatiha according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS), through the unbroken chain of all twelve Imams going back to Imam al-Hasan (AS), declares that Bismillah is a verse of Surah al-Fatiha. He quotes the Prophet (SAWW) who said that God favoured him with al-Fatiha, placing it equal to the rest of the Quran. This chain -- known as the 'silsilat al-dhahab' (golden chain) because every link is an infallible Imam -- was particularly valued in the circles of Shaykh al-Saduq. The hadith was transmitted during the Friday assembly in Muharram 368 AH and concludes with an exhortation about immense reward for reciting al-Fatiha with true belief in the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Yusuf b. Muhammad b. Ziyad and `Ali b. Muhammad b. Sayyar narrated to me from their father from al-Hasan b. `Ali from his father `Ali b. Muhammad from his father Muhammad b. `Ali from his father al-Rida `Ali b. Musa from his father Musa b. Ja`far from his father Ja`far b. Muhammad form his father Muhammad b. `Ali from his father `Ali b. al-Husayn from his father al-Husayn b.`Ali from his brother al-Hasan b. `Ali (as).

He said: Amir al-Mu’minin (as) said: Surely, “In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful” [1:1] is a verse from the Fatiha of the Book. It is seven verses, the best of which is “In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.” [1:1] I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: Surely, Allah said to me: O Muhammad! “We have given you the Seven Oft-Coupled verses and the Great Qur’an” [15:87], so be grateful to Me through the Fatiha of the Book and put it at the beginning of the Great Qur’an.

Surely, the Fatiha of the Book is more honourable than the treasures of the Throne. Surely, Allah has chosen Muhammad and honoured him with it, and no prophet shares [any of] that honour except Sulayman (as), for he was given “In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful” [27:30], which is seen in the story of Balqis, who said, “It is from Sulayman, and it reads: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.” [27:30].

Surely, whomever recites it, whilst aligned with Muhammad and his Righteous Family, acting by their orders, and believing in their apparent and esoteric [teachings], Allah will give him a deed for every letter: each of which is better than this world and everything in it, from its wealth to its goodness. Whomever listens to a reciter who recites it will be given the same reward at the reciter. So, you should increase this good thing that has been given to you, for it is a treasure that does not disappear with time, and it will remain in your repentant hearts.
